title: FLB: Fine-grained Load Balancing for Lossless Datacenter Networks
problem: Existing fine-grained load balancing schemes designed for lossy datacenter networks are counterproductive in lossless environments with PFC (Priority Flow Control), causing head-of-line (HoL) blocking that worsens congestion rather than alleviates it.
motivation: Modern datacenters rely on RDMA/RoCE with PFC for lossless transmission and multiple parallel paths, but load balancing mechanisms need rethinking for this environment to avoid HoL blocking.
method: FLB employs threshold-free rerouting to balance traffic load and improve link utilization during normal operation, and uses timely congested flow isolation to eliminate HoL blocking on non-congested flows when congestion occurs. The scheme integrates with RDMA/RoCE and coordinates with PFC to avoid pathological rerouting patterns.
key_novelty: Threshold-free rerouting combined with congested flow isolation specifically designed to eliminate PFC head-of-line blocking while maintaining load balancing effectiveness.
contributions: Comprehensive analysis of PFC and load balancing interactions in lossless datacenter networks
Threshold-free rerouting mechanism that effectively balances load without triggering HoL blocking
Congested flow isolation technique to prevent HoL blocking on non-congested flows
Full prototype implementation with evaluation showing significant performance improvements

metrics.other: 96% PFC PAUSE rate reduction, up to 40% FCT reduction over baselines
